items.t: Japan unveils rover prototype for Moon water mission
items.d: Japan’s space agency yesterday unveiled a test model of a rover that will travel to the Moon’s south pole in a search for water, which could potentially be used for rocket fuel.

items.t: Bulgaria rescues 35 migrants from rubber boat in Black Sea
items.d: Bulgarian border police have intercepted 35 migrants trying to reach Bulgaria on board an inflatable boat in the Black Sea near the border with Turkey, the interior ministry said yesterday.

items.t: Up to 700,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war: leaked data
items.d: The Kremlin yesterday declined to comment on reports that up to 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in its almost five-year-long offensive on Ukraine.

items.t: Saudi-coalition strikes Yemen port city
items.d: Houthi media said early yesterday that Saudi forces had launched an attack on Yemen’s port city of Hodeida as the group threatened to target Jeddah and retaliate against the kingdom’s Red Sea ports.

items.t: Colombia rescues 20 hostages
items.d: Colombian security forces stormed a supermarket in the Caribbean city of Cartagena early yesterday, ending a day-long hostage siege, with the president saying all of those held had been rescued and one captor killed.

items.t: China’s space flight takes off with Pakistani national
items.d: China’s Shenzhou-24 space flight launched successfully yesterday morning, with its three-man crew including a Pakistani national, who will be the first foreign astronaut to board the Tiangong space station.

items.t: Greece cost-of-living strike hits trains and planes
items.d: Thousands of people demonstrated in Greek cities yesterday during a 24-hour cost-of-living strike that disrupted public transport and other services.

items.t: CIA hit by hack impacting unclassified info
items.d: The CIA and Office of the Director of National Intelligence suffered an apparent hack affecting unclassified information, four sources familiar with the matter told CNN.

items.t: Three dead, 23 missing after flooding
items.d: At least three workers were killed and 23 still missing after a gold mine on Indonesia’s Java island flooded following heavy rain, local authorities said yesterday.

items.t: Govt’s bank borrowing surges 72% in Jul-Sept as revenue falls short
items.d: The government’s reliance on bank borrowing to finance its budget increased sharply in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026-27 as revenue collection fell short of the target, raising concerns about the impact on private investment, inflation and development spending.

items.t: Banks consider turning GPH Ispat loans into bonds
items.d: Around two dozen banks are exploring an alternative to loan rescheduling to rescue GPH Ispat, a steelmaker struggling under liabilities of about Tk 12,000 crore as business slumps.

items.t: Banking reforms welcome, but political will is key
items.d: Banking is one of the biggest problems facing the country’s economy. Its troubles began to deepen in the final months of the Awami League government.

items.t: Turkish group Sanko plans $300m denim factory
items.d: Turkish industrial conglomerate Sanko Holding, through its denim division ISKO, plans to invest $300 million in a denim manufacturing plant at the Shreehatta Economic Zone in Moulvibazar in partnership with local conglomerate DBL Group.

items.t: Tk 1.73 lakh crore stuck in 47,500 cases of six state banks
items.d: Nearly 47,500 cases involving unpaid loans of six state-owned banks are pending across the country, with about Tk 1.73 lakh crore tied up in them, according to internal Bangladesh Bank data.

items.t: Low garment prices erode productivity gains
items.d: Bangladesh must find ways to negotiate higher prices for its readymade garment (RMG) products in international markets, as persistently low prices offered by global buyers are eroding the gains from workers’ productivity, experts said yesterday.

items.t: Japan’s Maruhisa opens second factory
items.d: Japanese garment maker Maruhisa Group yesterday announced the official launch of its second factory in Bangladesh, in Narayanganj, which began production in October with a planned total investment of Tk 100 crore.

items.t: Moribund capital market: How responsible is it for bank defaults?
items.d: Behind every dishonoured cheque stands a depositor who trusted a bank with their savings. Such bounced cheques, repeated protests by depositors and the merger of several banks, particularly shariah-based ones, under schemes devised by Bangladesh Bank are the visible face of the loan-default crisis.

items.t: Brent drops to $91
items.d: Crude oil prices steadied on Wednesday as the prospect of a market surplus offset concerns about disruptions to oil exports in the Middle East.

items.t: Heidelberg turns to Olympic Cement to expand in south
items.d: Cement manufacturer Heidelberg Materials Bangladesh will outsource production to Barishal-based Olympic Cement, in a bid to expand its reach in southern Bangladesh, speed up deliveries and reduce transportation costs.
